Q: How should token expiry, key rotation and logout work together?
A: Signature verification proves a token was signed by an accepted key under the selected algorithm; it does not alone prove issuer, audience, validity interval or current permission. Key rotation needs a controlled overlap and refresh policy. Logout of a browser session is different from immediate invalidation of every copied bearer token. Choose short validity, server-side revocation or another explicit session policy according to the threat and latency requirements. Never let a client select arbitrary verification algorithms or trusted keys.
Why: Removing a token from local browser storage does not invalidate an attacker-held copy. If immediate revocation is required, the backend needs a revocation or session-state check rather than relying only on expiration.
Risk: Cached key or permission state can extend an unintended acceptance window.
Trade: Stateless validation reduces lookups but complicates immediate revocation.
Try: Trace a stolen token through logout, permission removal, key rotation and expiry.
worked_case: Removing a token from local browser storage does not invalidate an attacker-held copy. If immediate revocation is required, the backend needs a revocation or session-state check rather than relying only on expiration.
